data_scope.data_type: simulated PDE fields only; no observational or survey data
data_scope.primary_task: Navier-Stokes: map forcing function to vorticity at a later time from zero initial vorticity
data_scope.secondary_task: Darcy flow: map pressure to forcing at fixed diffusion coefficient (Supplementary F.2)
data_scope.cross_resolution_protocol: identical learned parameters evaluated at unseen lower and higher resolutions, no retraining or fine-tuning
data_scope.metric: relative L2 error on unseen test data (trained on absolute L2)
data_scope.optimizer: Adam with model-specific learning-rate schedules and weight decay
data_scope.sample_counts: not stated in the main text; deferred to Supplementary Sections F.1-F.3

core_conclusion: Neural networks learn maps between finite-dimensional arrays, while most scientific data are discretized samples of continuous fields. The paper distils three principles for function-space learning (discretization agnosticism, fixed parameter count, universal approximation) and gives a minimal recipe for converting MLPs, CNNs, GNNs, transformers and encoder-decoders into neural operators: replace index-based parameters with coordinate-dependent kernels, replace index sums with quadrature-weighted integrals over coordinate-defined neighbourhoods, and make latent interfaces independent of the observation grid. On Navier-Stokes, FNO and OFORMER trained only at resolution 128 generalize to unseen coarser and finer resolutions, whereas U-Net and ViT degrade; mixed-resolution training helps only at resolutions actually seen.
why_it_matters: Turns 'neural operator' from a model family into a reusable design rule; diagnoses resolution failure as an architectural defect rather than a data problem (a U-Net accepts any array size but silently implements a different operation at a new resolution); rehabilitates quadrature weights as a first-class modelling object, since uniform aggregation over irregular points has no unique limit under refinement; and keeps operator learning coupled to mainstream architectural progress via layer-local conversions, shipped in the open neuraloperator library with archived data and code.
why_nature: Perspective-shaped reframing backed by a controlled cross-resolution experiment; cross-cutting methodology applicable to fluids, climate, mechanics and imaging rather than a single benchmark win; bridges numerical analysis (quadrature, discretization error, convergence) with deep-learning architecture design; honest about the fixed-resolution accuracy cost and about open problems (error estimates, complex geometries, efficient high-resolution attention); fully open-science (CC-BY, open library, Zenodo data and code).
added_value_to_my_research: Quadrature weights reframe MAUP as numerical analysis -> population/area-weighted aggregation with a scale-consistency check for KDE and exposure surfaces
2SFCA/R2SFCA rewritten as the paper's integral-kernel layer -> learnable distance-decay and a principled fixed-radius vs kNN catchment argument
Two-axis protocol separating discretization error from conditional shift -> cleaner spatial transferability ablations and a companion diagnostic for MGWR non-stationarity
Boundary-aware operator layers for domains with holes, coastlines and moving boundaries -> barrier-respecting urban exposure and accessibility surfaces
Operator-ifying patch-tokenized geospatial foundation models -> multi-resolution sensor fusion without resampling to a lowest common denominator
